auth.withMicrosoft: Use the Microsoft 365 account you already sign in to email with. SUPSERV keeps no password of its own.
auth.failed: Sign-in did not complete. Nothing was changed — try again.
auth.noAccountHelp: Only accounts in the SUPSERV directory can sign in. If yours is refused, ask the Gérant to add you.
auth.noRoleTitle: Your account works, but you have no access yet
auth.noRoleBody: You are signed in as {email}. The Gérant decides what each person may do, and has not assigned you a role. Nothing is broken — ask them to open Settings → Users and roles.

profile.title: My profile
profile.subtitle: Settings that follow you, not the company.
profile.interfaceLanguageHelp: This changes what YOU see. It does not change the language of any document or email — those follow the client or supplier they are addressed to.
profile.documentLanguageHelp: Set on each company, not here. A French client receives French paperwork even when you work in English.

filters.stageHint: More than one value allowed — OR inside a field
filters.ownerHint: AND between fields, OR inside one

views.closingThisWeekAsks: Deadline inside 7 days, not won or lost
views.waitingOnSupplierAsks: Asked, no reply, 2 days or more
views.nothingSentYetAsks: Enquiry open, no offer, older than 3 days

search.title: Search
search.prompt: Companies, contacts, items and references. Spelling does not have to be exact.
search.noneBody: Try fewer words, or part of a name. If a company is known here by another spelling, add it as an alias on its page and every future search will find it.
search.notLookedYet: Search looks in four places: records, documents we generated, files we received, and email bodies. Only records exist so far — the other three are not empty, they have not been looked in yet.

company.newSubtitle: Only the legal name and one role are required. The rest can follow.
company.identityHelp: The name on their paperwork, and what they are to us.
company.tradeNameHint: If they are known by something shorter. Saved as an alias so search finds it.
company.rolesHint: A company can be both a client and a supplier. The first one chosen sets the code.
company.legalIdentityHelp: Décret 05-468 requires the client's NIF on an invoice, alongside our own RC, NIF, NIS and article d'imposition. Leave them empty now if you do not have them — the invoice will say what is missing when the time comes.
company.docLocaleHelp: Documents and email follow the COMPANY, not the person writing. Set French here and this client receives French paperwork even when an English-speaking colleague produces it.
company.aliasHelp: Every spelling anyone has used. Search matches all of them, and a merge adds the retired company's names here.
company.noContacts: Nobody recorded at this company yet.

bin.title: Deleted
bin.subtitle: Restorable for 30 days. After that the record is gone but its audit trail is not.
bin.emptyBody: Anything you remove lands here first, with who removed it and why.
bin.reasonPlaceholder: Why is it going? This is kept.
bin.removingHelp: Discard puts it in the bin for 30 days — for a record that should never have existed. Archive keeps it and every document that points at it, but takes it out of lists and search — for a client you no longer work with. An issued document is never deleted by either: it is cancelled, and an avoir keeps the number.
bin.blockedByIssued: This company has issued documents, so it cannot be discarded — a sent invoice must keep resolving. Archive it instead: it leaves the lists and every document still works.
bin.goneBody: Removed on {date}. You have {days} days to bring it back.
bin.afterThirtyDays: After 30 days the record is removed but the audit entry stays. In two years you can still find out that it existed and why it went.

empty.noCompaniesBody: Companies arrive when you add one, or when an email from a new sender is filed against a new record.
empty.noDealsBody: Deals appear here when you create one, or when an email in the Inbox is turned into one.
empty.errorBody: The server did not respond. Nothing was changed.
empty.noPermissionTitle: You do not have access to cost and margin
empty.noPermissionBody: The rest of this offer is visible. Ask the Gérant for {permission}.

invoice.companyIdentityIncomplete: Company identity is incomplete — RC, NIF, NIS or article d'imposition
invoice.vatServicesAbroad: VAT on services rendered abroad not confirmed

rules.unconfirmed: This rule has not been confirmed yet. It warns rather than blocks.
rules.comingInPhase: Not built yet — this arrives in phase {phase}.

merge.title: Merge duplicates
merge.subtitle: Two records, one company · you choose field by field, and nothing is lost
merge.duplicatesSubtitle: Two records that look like one company. Suggested, never automatic.
merge.noneBody: No two companies share a registration number, a tax number, an email domain, or a name close enough to flag. Pairs you have dismissed are not suggested again.
merge.leftIsKept: the left one is kept, and it keeps its reference

note.aliases: Both lists are kept — aliases are never a choice, they are added together. The retired code and name join them, so the old reference stays searchable.
note.nif: Fifteen digits. Often only one of the two records has them.
note.rcIdentical: Identical — this is why the system flagged them.
note.email: The other one becomes a contact rather than being thrown away.
note.paymentTerms: The newer record is proposed — it came off the last signed contract.

merge.nothingDropped: nothing is dropped, nothing is duplicated
merge.nothingAttached: Nothing is attached to either record yet. Documents, contacts and files appear here as they arrive.
merge.auditNote: Audit entries are not moved either — both trails are kept, and the merge itself is written into them: who, when, and every field chosen.

signalYes.similarName: after accents and spacing are stripped

merge.suggestedBody: Two companies can share a phone number and be genuinely different. The system proposes; a person decides. Not a duplicate is remembered, so the same pair is never suggested again.
merge.notADeleteTitle: A merge is not a delete
merge.notADeleteBody: {code} is retired, not removed. Every document that was ever issued under it keeps its number and still resolves. Nobody has to explain a missing reference to a client two years from now.

fourPlaces.contacts: the same person in two companies

merge.fourPlacesBody: One merge screen, four entities. Building it once is the difference between a tidy database and the Excel files this system replaces.
merge.banner: {count, plural, =1 {One pair of companies looks like the same client.} other {# pairs of companies look like the same client.}}

contacts.subtitle: {people} people at {companies} companies · {unverified} unverified · {bouncing, plural, =0 {no bouncing addresses} =1 {1 email bouncing} other {# emails bouncing}}
contacts.bouncingNeverReached: {count, plural, =1 {One email address is bouncing.} other {# email addresses are bouncing.}} {company} has never replied to a request — not because they are slow, but because nothing has ever reached them.
contacts.bouncingKnown: {count, plural, =1 {One email address is bouncing.} other {# email addresses are bouncing.}} Mail to {company} is coming back, so anything sent since is unread.
contacts.name: Name
contacts.jobHint: What they do at that company — Purchasing, Project manager, Legal.
contacts.prefersHint: How they answer fastest. Leave blank until you know.
contacts.emptyBody: A contact is a person at another company. Add the first one, or bring them in with the companies when the Excel move-in arrives.
contacts.whyOwnScreenTitle: Why this is its own screen
contacts.whyOwnScreenBody: A contact belongs to a company, but you deal with people. When a deadline is in six hours you search a name, not a company. And a person moves — the same buyer appears at a new employer and everything they told you should follow them.
contacts.newSubtitle: A name, a job, and the company they work for. The rest can wait.
contacts.newVerifyNote: A new contact starts as unverified — nobody has confirmed the address reaches them yet. It turns active the first time they reply.

error.jobRequired: Say what they do at that company — it is how you will find them later.
error.companyRequired: A contact belongs to a company. Choose one.
error.emailInvalid: That email address does not look right.
error.invalid: Something in the form was not accepted.

people.subtitle: {total, plural, =1 {1 person} other {# people}} · {fromCv} came from a CV, {rest} did not · a CV is evidence, not a requirement
people.directlyBanner: A person can be created directly — a name and a trade is enough. Day labourers, a subcontractor's welder, a driver hired for a week: none of them will ever send a CV, and all of them can be put on a project.
people.name: Name
people.tradePlaceholder: Soudeur, Électricien BT, Chef de chantier
people.emptyBody: A name and a trade is enough to start. The first person you add can be the driver you hired this morning.

origin.cv: A CV that arrived by any channel

people.whereFromBody: The candidate bank is one source of people, not the definition of one. A person exists in their own right; a CV, a certification and an ID copy are documents attached to them.

applies.project: Can be put on a project
applies.moyensHumains: Counts in moyens humains for a bid

error.tradeRequired: A trade is the second required field — Soudeur, Manœuvre, Chauffeur.
error.invalid: Something in the form was not accepted.

intake.channelsSubtitle: {total} ways work reaches SUPSERV · {live} are live · {losing, plural, =0 {none are losing records} =1 {1 is losing records today} other {# are losing records today}}
intake.losingRecords: The portal and paper channels have no path into the system. Anything arriving that way exists only in somebody's memory until it is typed in by hand.
intake.mailboxNotReading: The mailbox is not being read

channelAccepts.phone_note: A person writes down a call

intake.firstMatchWins: applied in order, first match wins

rule.cvFromStranger: Attachment is a CV and sender is not a known company
rule.rfq: Subject contains PR / RFQ / demande de cotation
rule.rfqAction: Enquiry, linked to the sender's company
rule.tender: Subject contains consultation / avis / appel d'offres
rule.supplierPrice: Sender is a known supplier and body contains a price
rule.supplierPriceAction: Supplier quote, attach to the open enquiry
rule.paymentAction: Payment, match against an open invoice

intake.sameAsAssistant: the same rules the assistant obeys

rail.neverAutoReply: Nothing is auto-replied to a client
rail.originalKept: Original email kept as the archive
rail.unmatchedToReview: Unmatched mail goes to Needs review

intake.railsNote: Enforced means there is no setting. Those three are constants in the code, because the moment one becomes a switch is the moment somebody turns it off at six in the evening to get a batch through.

inbox.subtitle: {unread} unread · {expiring, plural, =0 {nothing has a deadline inside 48 hours} =1 {1 item with a deadline inside 48 hours} other {# items with a deadline inside 48 hours}}
inbox.synced: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing new.} =1 {1 new message.} other {# new messages.}}

error.mailboxNotScoped: The mailbox was not read, because the application is not yet restricted to it. Application Mail.Read reaches every mailbox in the tenant until an Application Access Policy says otherwise.
error.tradeRequired: A candidate needs a trade — it is what you will search by.

inbox.expiringBanner: {count, plural, =1 {1 item expires} other {# items expire}} within 48 hours —
inbox.subject: Subject
inbox.deadlineUnconfirmedHelp: Read from the document, not yet confirmed by anybody. It warns; nothing relies on it.
inbox.emptyBody: Everything that arrived has been dealt with. New mail appears here when the mailbox is synced.
inbox.needsAHuman: Not classified with confidence — needs a human
inbox.notSureEnough: looks like a {what}, but only {percent}% sure — so nothing was created

moveIn.title: Move in
moveIn.subtitle: bring what you already have · nothing of yours is changed or deleted
moveIn.filesStay: Your Excel files stay exactly where they are. This copies what is useful into the system and tells you what it could not read.
moveIn.chooseBody: One spreadsheet at a time. A list of clients, a list of suppliers, or a staff list — the columns are read and matched, and anything unrecognised is left alone.
moveIn.oneDriveLater: Reading your OneDrive folders directly needs the same Microsoft permission conversation as the mailbox, and is not connected yet. Until then, upload the file.
moveIn.mappedOf: {mapped} of {total} mapped · the rest are ignored
moveIn.alreadyImported: This file has already been imported.
moveIn.noProblems: Nothing in this file needed handling.

problem.badNif: NIF that is not fifteen digits

moveIn.keepUsingExcel: You can keep working in Excel for a while afterwards. Most people stop within a month because the system already has the answer.
moveIn.onlyWhatFitsTitle: Only what has somewhere to go
moveIn.onlyWhatFitsBody: Companies, contacts and people are imported today. Deals, offers, invoices and payments arrive with the phases that build them — importing them into tables that do not exist yet would lose them twice.
moveIn.imported: {count, plural, =1 {1 record created.} other {# records created.}} You can undo this for {days} days.
moveIn.undone: {count, plural, =1 {1 record sent to the bin.} other {# records sent to the bin.}}{kept, plural, =0 {} =1 { 1 was kept, because a document has been issued against it since.} other { # were kept, because documents have been issued against them since.}}

error.emptySheet: That file has no table in it that could be read.
error.unreadable: That file could not be read as a spreadsheet.
error.noBatch: That import is no longer available.
error.undoExpired: The seven days are up — this import can no longer be undone in one step.

review.title: Review what we read — {file}, page {page} of {pages}
review.subtitle: {done} of {total} confirmed · nothing is saved until you confirm
review.becomesFact: This is the only place extraction becomes fact. A wrong deadline or a missing document on this list loses the bid — so a person confirms every field against the page it came from.
review.confirmedCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing was confident enough to confirm on its own.} =1 {1 field confirmed.} other {# fields confirmed.}}
review.unreadPages: {count, plural, =1 {Page {pages} could not be read} other {Pages {pages} could not be read}} — they are scans, and the OCR step is not running on this machine yet. Everything else on this screen came from pages that were read.
review.pageNotRead: Page {page} is a scan. There is no text to show until OCR runs.
review.confirmCorrectReject: confirm, correct, or reject each one
review.nothingRead: Nothing was read from this document that matches a field we know how to check. That is a result, not a failure — the file is stored and can be read again once the rules know what to look for.

caveat.severalCandidates: the document says this more than once
caveat.sameDayAsDeadline: the day comes from the deadline, the time from this sentence
caveat.dayUnknown: the time is clear, the day is not

dossier.title: Read a document
dossier.subtitle: a PDF goes in, and what it says comes out — with the page it said it on
dossier.textLayerFirst: A digital PDF is read from its own text layer: instant, exact, and nothing leaves this machine. A scanned one needs OCR, which runs in a container that is not set up yet — those pages are named rather than guessed at.

setup.title: Day one
setup.subtitle: the empty system · eleven things to set before the first document can be issued
setup.canIssue: The first four are done. A document can be issued.
setup.cannotIssue: Until these are done, no invoice can be issued at all: {missing}. This is not a warning — the number allocator refuses.

step.identity: Company identity — name, address, RC, NIF, NIS, article d'imposition
step.numbering: Numbering series — invoices, offers, delivery notes
step.stampDuty: Droit de timbre — when it applies
step.paymentTerms: Payment terms and the default currency
step.roles: People and roles — who may see cost and margin
step.storage: Storage — where every file is filed
step.moveIn: Bring in what you already have

why.identity: Décret 05-468 requires them on every invoice
why.logo: Every generated document reads it from here
why.vat: A line cannot be priced without one
why.numbering: A number is allocated at issue and never reused
why.bank: Printed on the invoice as the domiciliation
why.paymentTerms: Fills the offer and the invoice
why.roles: Everyone is Gérant until you say otherwise
why.mailbox: Nothing arrives in the Inbox until this is done
why.moveIn: Companies, contacts and people from Excel

setup.readFromLater: Where each answer is read from later
setup.typedOnceBody: No template holds your address. Change the logo in one place and every template changes with it.
setup.willNotInvent: What the system will not invent for you

notInvent.identityBody: RC, NIF, NIS and the article d'imposition are typed once, by you, and checked against the paper. Nothing else in the system can be trusted if these are wrong.
notInvent.numberingBody: SUP/2026/0001 or FA-2026-001 — the shape is yours. Once the first document is issued the shape is frozen for the year, because a series with two shapes in it is a series nobody can defend.
notInvent.ratesBody: 19 % and 9 % are today's figures, entered as rules with a start date. When they change you add a new rate rather than editing the old one, so last year's invoices still recompute correctly.

setup.fourRules: The four rules waiting on your accountant
setup.fourRulesBody: The system never asserts a legal rule on its own authority. Each one names its source, who confirmed it and when. Until somebody confirms these four, the system warns and lets you proceed.
setup.emptiestDay: Day one is also the emptiest day
setup.everyListEmptyBody: And an empty list is the state most people meet first. Each one gives a sentence saying what belongs there and the button that creates the first record.
setup.noFakeDataTitle: Nothing is demonstrated with fake data
setup.noFakeDataBody: A system that ships with sample companies teaches people to ignore what is on screen. The lists stay empty until you put something real in them.
setup.identitySubtitle: typed once, by you, and checked against the paper
setup.decret: Décret exécutif 05-468 requires the RC, NIF, NIS and article d'imposition on every invoice. Three of the four is not partly compliant — it is an invoice that cannot be issued.
setup.logoBody: Read by every generated document. Change it here and every template changes with it — no template holds its own copy.
setup.logoOnFile: A logo is already on file. Choosing another replaces it.
setup.vatSubtitle: rates are rules with a start date, not a setting
setup.noRatesYet: No rate has been entered yet. A line cannot be priced without one.
setup.rateAdded: Rate added. The one it replaces keeps its dates.
setup.noEditButton: There is no edit button, and that is the feature. Adding a rate closes the one before it; the old row keeps its dates, so every document already issued still recomputes to the same total.
setup.numberingSubtitle: the shape is yours, and it is frozen once the first document is issued
setup.frozenBody: Once the first document is issued the shape is frozen for the year, because a series with two shapes in it is a series nobody can defend. Change it in January, not in June.
setup.noSeriesYet: No series yet. A document cannot be issued without one.
setup.reservedAtIssue: A number is allocated at issue and never on a draft, so a draft that is abandoned leaves no gap in the series.
setup.patternExamples: {a} and {b} are both valid. Use {'{'}YYYY{'}'} for the year and {'{'}####{'}'} for the counter.
setup.bankSubtitle: printed on the invoice as the domiciliation

h.nif: Fifteen digits, from the carte fiscale
h.authority: The text this rate comes from — a rate with no source is somebody's memory
h.pattern: Must contain a year and a counter
h.rib: Twenty digits, exactly as printed. A wrong digit is a payment that goes elsewhere.

error.aiRequired: The article d'imposition is required — décret 05-468.
error.addressRequired: The address is printed on every document.
error.emailInvalid: That email address does not look right.
error.rateInvalid: A rate is a number, and a start date is required.
error.patternNeedsCounter: The pattern needs a counter, like {'{'}####{'}'}.
error.patternNeedsYear: The pattern needs a year, like {'{'}YYYY{'}'}.
error.invalid: Something in the form was not accepted.

documents.sendUnavailable: Sending is not available yet — the shared mailbox has not been scoped to a single account.
documents.issuedOk: Issued as {number}. It can no longer be edited — a correction is a new document.
documents.alreadyIssued: Already issued. An issued document is immutable; a correction is a new one.
documents.notAllowed: Your role may not issue this kind of document.
documents.ruleUnconfirmed: Rule from {authority}, not confirmed by anyone yet — it warns rather than blocks.
documents.previewUnavailable: Your browser will not display the PDF here.
documents.localeFromClient: The language of a document comes from the client record, never from whoever is signed in.

error.notAllowed: Your role may not issue this kind of document.
error.setupIncomplete: Day one is not finished, so nothing can be issued yet.
error.alreadyIssued: That document has already been issued.
error.blocked: A confirmed rule refused this document
error.complianceBlocked: A confirmed rule refused this document.

checklist.title: Before issuing
checklist.summary: {blockers, plural, =0 {no blocker} one {# blocker} other {# blockers}} · {warnings, plural, =0 {no warning} one {# warning} other {# warnings}}
checklist.footnote: Green means we looked and it was there. Only a rule somebody has confirmed can refuse an issue; the rest warn.

note.notRecorded: Not recorded — nothing will be printed
note.numberOnIssue: Reserved on issue, never on a draft

newInvoice.title: New invoice
newInvoice.subtitle: Nothing is known yet, so this one is typed. Later ones start from an order.

start.laterReason: Starting from an order, an offer or a situation needs those records to exist. They arrive with the sales modules; until then an invoice is typed.

newInvoice.dateHint: The date that goes on the document. Today unless you change it.
newInvoice.languageFrom: This document will be written in {language} — that comes from the client.
newInvoice.clientHasNoNif: This client has no NIF recorded. You can draft, but not issue.
newInvoice.linesHint: A line with no description or no quantity is not saved
newInvoice.stampDutyLater: Stamp duty is not added here. It applies to cash settlement, and the rule is one of the four still waiting on the accountant.
newInvoice.noNumberYet: No number is taken yet — that happens when you issue.

saveStep.draft: A draft is created. Nothing is sent and nothing is registered.
saveStep.number: No invoice number is reserved. Drafts never consume one.
saveStep.preview: You land on the document, with the PDF the client would receive.
saveStep.issue: Issuing is a separate, deliberate act — and it cannot be undone.

newInvoice.notHereYetBody: Discounts, advances, retenue de garantie, option lines and section headings are in the schema but have no controls on this screen. They arrive with the full document builder.
newInvoice.noClientsYet: There are no companies yet, so there is nobody to invoice.
newInvoice.setupWarning: You can draft this invoice, but not issue it yet: {missing} still to do.

error.notAllowed: Your role may not create invoices.
error.noLines: An invoice needs at least one line with a description and a quantity.

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.subtitle: {unpaid, plural, =0 {nothing unpaid} one {# unpaid} other {# unpaid}} · {outstanding} outstanding · overdue is computed from the due date, not stored
invoices.exportLater: Export arrives with the reports module.
invoices.proformaLater: A proforma needs its own numbering series and its own validity rule. Both are still to be set up.
invoices.paymentsLater: There is no Paid column and no relance banner because payments are not recorded yet. Overdue is worked out from the due date and the balance whenever this page loads — it is never a status somebody sets.

users.title: Users and roles
users.subtitle: {users, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} · {roles} roles · permissions apply everywhere, not only in the interface
users.inviteUnavailable: There is nothing to send. A colleague appears in this list the first time they sign in with their Microsoft account — and arrives with no role until you give them one.
users.noPasswords: sign-in is handled by Microsoft 365 — no passwords are stored here
users.saved: Role changed. The audit log has who did it and when.
users.withoutRole: {count, plural, one {# person has signed in and has no role} other {# people have signed in and have no role}}. They can see nothing until you give them one.
users.readOnly: only the Gérant can change this
users.howPeopleAppear: Nobody is created on this screen. Entra decides who exists; this decides what they may do, and the two never touch.
users.whyReadOnly: This table is the only thing standing between a person and data they may not see, so it lives in src/auth/can.ts rather than in a grid of checkboxes: a change goes through a commit, is reviewed, and is visible in the history. A mis-click here would be silent.

error.notAllowed: Only a Gérant may change roles.
error.self: You cannot change your own role. Ask another Gérant.
error.lastGerant: This is the last Gérant. Give somebody else that role first, or the system locks with nobody able to unlock it.
error.unknownRole: That is not a role this system knows.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: The company, the money, the documents and what comes in
settings.cannotIssue: No document can be issued yet: {missing} still to do. Everything else on this page works without them.

identity.name: Legal identity
identity.what: Legal name, RC, NIF, NIS, article d'imposition, address. Printed on every document.

logo.name: Logo
logo.what: One file. Change it once and every document changes.

bank.name: Bank accounts
bank.what: RIB and domiciliation. The default one prints on invoices.

vat.name: VAT rates
vat.what: Each rate with the date it started. Old documents keep the old rate.

numbering.name: Numbering
numbering.what: One series per document kind. Changing a pattern never renumbers what is already issued.

users.name: Users and roles
users.what: Who has signed in, and what each of them may do.

profile.name: My profile
profile.what: Your own interface language and preferences.

language.name: Language
language.what: The language you work in, and the language each client is written to in.

channels.name: Channels
channels.what: The mailbox, the scan station, the website forms.

import.name: Move in from Excel
import.what: Read a file, preview it, import it, undo within 7 days.

storage.name: Storage
storage.unbuilt: Needs Graph Files.ReadWrite scoped to one SharePoint site — the same conversation as the mailbox, and it has not been had. Documents go to the working volume until then.

compliance.name: Compliance rules
compliance.what: Confirm a rule and it starts refusing.
compliance.unbuilt: Screen 69. The four unconfirmed rules are listed on the day-one checklist and warn on every document; confirming one needs this screen, which is not built.

bin.name: Deleted and restore
bin.what: The 30-day bin. Nothing is removed before it expires.

audit.name: Audit log
audit.unbuilt: Every action already writes an entry — screens 18, 30, 62 and 70 all do. The page that reads them back is not built.

language.title: Language
language.subtitle: Two settings that never touch each other: the language you work in, and the language a document goes out in.
language.banner: The interface follows the person. Documents and email follow the client or the supplier. You can work in English and still send a French invoice to an Algerian client — and you cannot do it the other way round by accident, because neither setting can reach the other.
language.perPersonWhat: menus, buttons, tables and validation messages only
language.perCounterpartyWhat: what the client reads, or what the supplier understands
language.noCounterparties: No companies yet, so nothing has a document language.
language.changeOnTheRecord: Changed on the company record, not here. A second place to set it would be a second answer to which language a document is in.
language.rules: What the system actually does about language
language.notEnforced: not enforced — no confirmed rule behind it
language.whyNotEnforced: The greyed rows are claims about the law, or about what an authority requires. Nobody has confirmed them, so the system does not act on them — it would be asserting a rule on its own authority. Confirm one on the compliance screen and it starts refusing.

rule.documentFollowsCounterparty: A document is written in the counterparty's language, never in the language of whoever pressed the button
rule.amountInWords: The amount in words is generated in the document's language
rule.formatFollowsDocument: Dates and numbers on a document follow the document, not the reader
rule.interfaceFollowsPerson: The interface follows the person signed in
rule.neverTranslated: Legal names, identifiers and references are never translated
rule.algerianInvoiceLanguage: An invoice to an Algerian client must be French or Arabic
rule.tenderLanguage: A tender submission follows the language the authority requires

language.counted: Counted from the message files when this page loads, not written down. If somebody adds an English string and forgets the French one, this number drops.

never.legalNames: Legal names of companies — as registered
never.identifiers: NIF, NIS, RC, AI — identifiers, not words
never.references: Item references — as the client wrote them
never.original: The original email or file — that is the archive
never.numbers: Numbers already issued — SUP/2026/0041 stays SUP/2026/0041

language.neverTranslatedWhy: Translating a legal name or a reference would make a document wrong. The system stores what was written and shows it unchanged in both languages.
language.arabicBody: Not built. The interface has no Arabic strings and no right-to-left layout, and no document template is written in Arabic. It is listed here so the gap is visible rather than discovered.
